title: Feature Selection for Network Intrusion Detection

problem.claim: Network intrusion detection models use network features extracted from raw data, but irrelevant or noisy features can increase resource use and impair attack detection.

gap.claim: PCA can reduce dimensionality but cannot assess feature relevance for the detection task.

contributions.claim: FSNID is an information-theoretic method for excluding non-informative features during network intrusion detection.
The method uses function approximation with a neural network and has a version incorporating a recurrent layer.
The recurrent version integrates temporal dependencies.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors describe FSNID as a novel method and state that its recurrent version uniquely enables integration of temporal dependencies.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments selected a significantly reduced feature set while maintaining network intrusion detection performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Network intrusion detection is important to information security and machine learning practitioners.
Common feature extraction and dimensionality reduction can leave irrelevant features, creating resource and detection-quality drawbacks.
The authors introduce FSNID, an information-theoretic feature-selection method with a neural-network formulation and recurrent variant.
The authors report experiments showing a reduced feature set with maintained detection performance.
The authors provide a code repository.
